profile.reading: Digital Fortress Lynnwood, marketed by the operator as its North Seattle data center, sits at 4200 194th Street Southwest, Lynnwood, Washington 98036. Per the operator's own site, fetched fresh, the facility has been operational since 2006, is designed to Tier 3 standards, is carrier neutral with 24 by 7 support, and provides 6 megawatts of power capacity, a figure independently corroborated by a third party aggregator, DataCenterMap. Digital Fortress, per trade press coverage on this registry's separate Meadowville, Virginia row, has operated since 1994, growing from nine facilities nationwide as a multi tenant and wholesale data center provider serving enterprises across multiple states including Washington, Oregon, Colorado, Illinois, New Jersey, and Virginia, and is a Chirisa Investments portfolio company. No specific square footage was found published for this Lynnwood building this session despite a fresh attempt, an honest gap; the operator's dedicated Lynnwood facility page on digital-fortress.com continues to return a not found error, so the figures here rest on the operator's broader North Seattle marketing page and independent aggregator corroboration rather than a single dedicated facility page. Lynnwood sits immediately north of Seattle in Snohomish County, Washington, a secondary Pacific Northwest data center market that has drawn colocation investment as an alternative to more expensive downtown Seattle real estate while remaining close enough for low latency access to the same carrier hotel infrastructure, including the Westin Building Exchange, that anchors the region's network connectivity. Digital Fortress's Pacific Northwest presence also includes three Portland and Beaverton, Oregon buildings already on file elsewhere in this registry, acquired from Atmosera in January 2021, giving the company a combined Seattle and Portland metro footprint alongside its East Coast Piscataway and Richmond facilities.

reading.body:
Digital Fortress Lynnwood publishes no power capacity, PUE, cooling system, or IT load specification. The facility's rank as third among published-capacity campuses in Washington state reflects the absence of disclosed figures from most of the state's 46 mapped data centers rather than a confirmed large footprint.

The operator has confirmed a presence in Snohomish County and Lynnwood through its own contact form, though the dedicated facility page on its website returns an error. The street address comes from an aggregator listing specific to this operator in this market. No certifications, tenancy, construction timeline, or grid connection details are published.

Washington state's two facilities with published capacity total 60 MW of disclosed power. Without a published figure for Lynnwood, the campus's actual scale and role in state or regional AI capacity cannot be determined from operator disclosure.
